newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to control regional Eurobond issues.
newsitem.headline: Russia to control regional Eurobond issues.

text.p: Russia, which launched a $1 billion debut Eurobond on Thursday, will head for capital markets again in 1997 but control issues by other Russian entitites following in its steps, Finance Minister Alexander Livshits said on Friday.
"We will do it next year, but of course it is premature to decide when," Livshits said, adding that the next bond could be in yen or other currencies.
He said the $1 billion bond, Russia's post-1917 revolution debut, was more than twice oversubscribed and would establish a benchmark for borrowing by regional authorities, cities, and companies.
"A door has opened for the regional governments... but we will regulate this process of regional governments applying to world markets...," he said.
"We do not want to close the door in their face after we have passed through it, but we do intend to limit access to the door."

Moscow, St Petersburg, Nizhny Novgorod and the Sverdlovsk area around Yekaterinburg all have projects to launch Eurobonds, and more municipalities and regional authorities are expected to follow. Several companies are also talking of Eurobond issues.
Russia has said it intends to borrow $1-2 billion on the Eurobond market next year.
Livshits said Russia should consider changing foreign borrowing limits in next year's budget, currently under consideration, but said the State Duma lower house of parliament would decide the issue.
He also said that the central bank's policy of limiting and regulating foreign access to Russia's domestic capital markets "could be affected by the success of yesterday's events".
